full_judgment:
Mr. Soumendra Sarker, J.:- The leave was granted to decide the question raised in connection with the impugned judgment and order dated 26.06.2008 passed by the learned District Judge, Faridpur in Civil Revision No.09 of 2006 filed by the plaintiff-petitioner against the judgment and order dated 28.03.2006 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Sadarpur, Faridpur in Title Execution Case No.11 of 2004, disallowing the Civil Revision affirming the aforesaid order of the learned Assistant Judge, Sadarpur, Faridpur. 

 2. The facts leading for granting leave in a nutshell can be stated thus, the petitioner as plaintiff instituted a Title Suit being No.22 of 2005 in the Court of the learned Assistant Judge, Sadarpur, Faridpur for partition, declaration & permanent injunction. The defendant-opposite parties obtained the decree of khash possession against the petitioner and started a Decree Execution Case No.11 of 2004. In a "Salish" the defendant-opposite parties agreed to withdraw the said execution Case but ultimately denied. For that reason the plaintiff-petitioner filed above mentioned suit being Title Suit No.22 of 2005 and filed an application with a prayer for staying further proceedings of Title Execution Case No.11 of 2004 till disposal of the Title Suit No.22 of 2005. 

 7. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the learned lst Revisional Court committed illegality in passing the impugned judgment and order and failed to apply his judicial mind to the facts that the petitioner filed a suit for partition as well as declaration challenging the judgment and decree passed in favour of the opposite-parties in Title Suit No.36 of 1997 from where the Decree Execution Case No.11 of 2004 arose. The learned Advocate further submits that the Courts below during passing their orders also committed an error of law in not giving the effect of the order dated 27.03.2005, rather misinterpreted the application for staying further proceedings of the Execution Case No.11 of 2004 and thereby committed error in law occasioning failure of justice. 

 9. Considering the submissions of the learned Advocates I have gone through the relevant papers alone with the application for staying further proceedings of Title Execution Case No.11 of 2004 pending in the Court of the learned Assistant Judge, Sadarpur, Faridpur. 

 10. Having gone through the application marked Annexure "A" it transpires that the plaintiff-petitioner specifically contended in the application that the decree passed in Title Suit No.36 of 1997 was obtained collusively which was not within his knowledge and in collusion with the process-server of the court the service return was made falsely and behind the back of the petitioner the decree dated 13.10.1997 was passed exparte against the plaintiff-petitioner showing his presence in the Suit. 

 11. It was further contended by the petitioner that in the locality there was a "Saliash" and in that "Salish" the matter-in-dispute has been amicably settled between the parties. Further More; the parties to the suits do reside in their respective homesteads, but the plaintiff therein who is the defendant No.1 of the petitioner's suit filed the Execution Case No.11 of 2004 to evict the plaintiff from his homestead. Finding no other alternative the plaintiff filed the suit for partition, declaration & injunction challenging the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.36 of 1997. That suit is Title Suit No.22 of 2005 in the concerned court of the learned Assistant Judge, Sadarpur, Faridpur against the present opposite parties. The present petitioner who instituted the Title Suit No.22 of 2005 before the learned Court below on 24.02.2005, have annexed herewith the certified copies of plaint (Annexure-A) of his suit wherein the relief with regard to the exparte decree passed in Title Suit. No.36 of 1997 was prayed for in paragraph "ঙ" of the prayer portion: In respect of the self-same suit property, that exparte decree which was obtained by the defendant No.1 who is the Opposite- party No.1 of this Civil Revision; has been challenged by this plaintiff-petitioner and the specific relief with regard to this; reads as follows: 

 12. It further transpires from the order of the trial court dated 27.03.2005 ( Annexure A-1) that the learned trial court being satisfied that the plaintiff have filed Title Suit No.22 of 2005 against the exparte judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.36 of 1997, stayed further proceedings of Title Execution Case No.11 of 2004. 

 13. Subsequently; the learned Trial Court vide his order dated 28.03.2006 in Title Execution Case No.11 of 2004 vacated his earlier order dated 27.03.2005 passed in Title Suit No.22 of 2005. 

 15. On perusal of the impugned judgment and order it appears that the learned 1st Revisional Court consulting the relevant papers arrived at a decision that admittedly against the petitioner Title Suit No.36 of 1997 was filed and in that suit the defendant made his appearance and also filed written statement engaging a learned Advocate therein but subsequently did not contest the Suit. Consequently, that Suit was decreed exparte. Pursuant to that exparte decree; Title Execution Case No.01 of 1998 was filed. Thereafter the present petitioner after filing the Title Suit being No.41 of 1998 prayed for staying further proceedings of Execution Case No.01 of 1998. The petitioner's Title Suit No.41 of 1998 was dismissed for his default. Thereafter; the petitioner again after filing a Title Suit No.07 of 1999 filed an application for staying further proceedings of Execution Case No.01 of 1998 and the learned Court stayed the proceedings of Execution Case No.01 of 1998. The Suit of the present petitioner was dismissed for his default and thereafter the decree-holder filed the Title Execution Case No.11 of 2004. The present petitioner instituting a Title Suit No.22 of 2005 stayed the operation of the judgment and decree of the defendant and the 14 Revisional Court also held that the present petitioner filed written statement in Title Suit No.36 of 1997 without filing an appeal against the judgment and decree. In this context; having gone through the contents of the plaint of Title Suit No.22 of 2005 filed by the present petitioner I have come across that the suit is pending in the Court of the learned Assistant Judge, Sadarpur, Faridpur in which the specific contention of the petitioner is such that in the suit property; the petitioner have residence/ homestead and that there was an amicable settlement by way of compromise between the parties in the locality which was subsequently violated by the present opposite party who managed to obtain an exparte decree against the petitioner on 13.10.1997. It was further contended by the petitioner therein that everything was suppressed and were behind his back collusively and thus the decree was fraudulent. 

 16. The allegation as stated by the petitioner was against the exparte decree passed against him and the proceeding of that Suit is also challenged from his side which is awaiting for disposal before a competent court of law. 

 17. Be that as it may; I have the reason to hold such a view that the learned lm Revisional Court as well as the Trial Court in rejecting the application for staying further proceedings of Title Execution Case No.11 of 2004 committed illegality. When the matter is subjudice before the learned Court below, it was the legal obligation of the courts to stay the execution proceedings of the decree which is under challenge. Having regard to the spelt out facts, circumstances and discussions referred to above I am constrained to hold such a view that the revisional application have got much merit to succeed. 

 18. In the result; the Civil Revision is allowed without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and order of the learned District Judge, Faridpur dated 26.06.2008 passed in Civil Revision No.09 of 2006 affirming those of dated 28.03.2006 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Sadarpur, Faridpur in Title execution Case No.11 of 2004 is hereby set-aside. 

 19. Let further proceedings of Title Execution Case No.11 of 2004 be stayed till disposal of Title Suit No.22 of 2005 pending in the court of Assistant Judge, Sadarpur, Faridpur.
